sources.title: Own axes/counts/smoothing derivations
sources.details: Batch shape [1,4] represents one context with four features or four candidate logits. Smoothing: 0.8*onehot+0.2/4 gives [0.85,0.05,0.05,0.05], and its logit gradient is p-target. Parameter formulas give 148, 241 and 97. There are 10*11/2=55 families and three modes per family; 44/5/6 families give 132/15/18 contexts. Each training family contributes 6+6+3=15 preference pairs, totaling 660. Draw arithmetic: 300*64=19,200; 120*64=7,680; 120*3=360 updates; 7,680*3=23,040 reused records. Saved greedy outputs were independently compared to the number/explain/missing rule.

claims.statement: Four structured features encode operands divided by 10 and the explain/missing indicators. Python prewrites the cards; the policy selects a card rather than reading Chinese, computing addition, or generating tokens.

evidence.supports: Original build_records constructs the four feature values, Python-computed candidate text and ideal action from the mode.
The actual small policy takes four numeric features and returns four logits; reward model combines numeric context with candidate identity, not Chinese text.
Executed data construction confirms the 1+2 feature vector, all four prewritten candidates and ideal action 0.

verification.expected: Expected features [0.1,0.2,0,0], four prewritten candidates and ideal action 0.
verification.observed: The generated example and network input/output matched exactly.
verification.details: No tokenizer or generation call occurs. Python constructs the candidate sums before model input.

claims.statement: Collect an action, its old log probability, reward, value and fixed advantage; recompute the same action with the current policy; optimize the PPO clipped surrogate and value prediction. The ratio is 1 before the first update.
claims.scope: A terminal, one-step contextual card recipe. This does not describe every detail of token-level RLHF.

evidence.locator: Section3 Eq6-7; Section5 Eq9-12 and Algorithm1 pp3-5
evidence.supports: Equations 6–7 define the same-action new/rollout-old probability ratio and clipped minimum surrogate; Algorithm 1 reuses a fixed collected batch over multiple optimization epochs. Equation 12 reduces to reward minus baseline for a terminal one-step task.
bandit_advantage detaches reward-minus-old-value and the PPO helper detaches old log probabilities and advantage before constructing the negative mean minimum surrogate.
The actual pre-step ratio was 1; after the same step it was 0.9300719499588013. All three recorded rollout quantities had requires_grad=False.

claims.statement: This recipe adds exact KL(policy || fixed reference) to the policy loss and MSE to the critic loss. Reward and reference stay frozen; critic estimates RM reward.
claims.scope: An explicitly specified finite-card recipe. Its fixed SFT reference differs from the old rollout policy; LLM implementations can treat rewards and value targets differently.

evidence.locator: Section3.5 RL paragraph and Eq2 pp6-7
evidence.supports: The RL paragraph and equation 2 support the conceptual RM reward with a fixed SFT-reference penalty. They do not prove this finite recipe is identical to token-level InstructGPT.
Equation 9 explicitly includes a squared value-target error term alongside the policy surrogate.
exact_kl sums p*(log p-log q) over all four candidates and detaches reference logits; the value network takes only context.
The original PPO loop adds its fixed-reference KL to policy loss, while the critic separately targets sampled normalized RM reward.

claims.statement: Categorical(logits) supplies card sampling and log probabilities; gather selects the chosen reward. no_grad fixes rollout records. zero_grad clears gradients, backward computes them, and SGD.step updates only the policy and critic parameters in its groups.
claims.location: 13.15: original Python fence and its explanation
claims.scope: Grouped sampling/indexing and autograd/optimizer contracts on installed PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu.

evidence.supports: Categorical normalizes logits on the last candidate axis, samples category indices and gathers their normalized log probabilities.
The original gather contract selects along axis 1 with [batch,1] indices, producing [batch,1] chosen rewards before squeeze.
no_grad disables graph recording for the collection arithmetic used here, so these computed rollout values stay fixed.
Module.requires_grad_ sets module parameter flags in place; applying False freezes RM/reference gradients.
Tensor.backward computes and accumulates graph-leaf gradients; its contract does not claim parameter updates.
Optimizer.zero_grad resets gradients only for tensors in the optimizer groups.
SGD.step updates the parameters and gradients collected from its own groups; excluded RM/reference parameters are not optimized.
Direct snapshots of all four networks prove policy and critic changed in both tested contexts, while RM/reference did not.

verification.expected: Policy and critic change; reward and reference do not; rollout records have no gradients.
verification.observed: Both the base example and third-feature variant matched these assertions; the optimizer contains eight parameter tensors.
verification.details: Executed the original fence verbatim. The instrumented variants snapshot all four networks before the same update. Personally read the core API contracts at the installed upstream commit.

claims.scope: Python 3.13.5 and PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu in the current environment; no cross-platform random-seed guarantee.

claims.statement: For four cards, label smoothing 0.2 mixes 80% of the original one-hot target with 20% uniform mass, producing [0.85,0.05,0.05,0.05]. This is a training target rather than a guaranteed prediction.
claims.scope: PyTorch uniform-mixture smoothing in this experiment. It is optional for SFT and does not guarantee exact output probabilities.

evidence.supports: The official cross_entropy contract says label_smoothing mixes the original target and a uniform distribution.
The original native implementation divides the smoothing mass by the number of classes, which is four here.
Independent target arithmetic yields .8*[1,0,0,0]+.2/4=[.85,.05,.05,.05]; derivative p-target gives positive target mass to the other cards rather than forcing model output equality.

evidence.locator: label_smoothing float64 loss and gradient check
evidence.supports: The float64 smoothed-loss and explicit soft-target calculations differ by less than 1e-12, and their gradient matches p-target.

verification.expected: The target is [0.85,0.05,0.05,0.05]; the smoothed loss equals the explicit soft-target loss.
verification.observed: Losses were 1.4667025112751417 and 1.4667025112751413. The gradient matched softmax minus the smoothed target.
verification.details: Used a nonuniform prediction to distinguish target from model output. Independently calculated 80% one-hot plus 5% for each class.
verification.tolerance: Absolute tolerance 1e-12 for float64 loss and gradient; the target arithmetic agrees exactly up to floating-point representation.

claims.scope: A distinction between this finite supervised example and LLM fine-tuning; the finite policy is not pretrained.

The finite policy is newly constructed before the demonstration cross-entropy loop, so this example starts from random initialization.

claims.statement: SFT uses 60 updates of 32 draws. RM uses 300 updates of 64 pairs, or 19,200 pair draws. PPO collects 120 batches of 64 fresh actions, or 7,680, and reuses each for three epochs: 360 policy updates, 360 critic updates and 23,040 reused action records. effective_tokens is 0 because this is a card task.
claims.scope: The original completed finite-card run. Resampled or reused records are distinguished from unique examples and fresh answers.

evidence.supports: Original CONFIG values and loops establish batch sizes, update counts and three optimization epochs per unchanged 64-action rollout; the task never trains token sequences.

Original saved configuration, final histories and count fields report completed 60/300/120 schedules, 360 updates per PPO network, 7,680 fresh actions, 23,040 reused records and zero effective tokens.
Own assertions recheck the count fields, final histories and three raw trace epochs; old probabilities, values, rewards and advantages stay unchanged across the 64-record reuse.
Independent multiplication verifies 60*32=1,920, 300*64=19,200, 120*64=7,680, 120*3=360, and 7,680*3=23,040; draws and tokens are distinct units.

verification.expected: 1,920 SFT draws; 19,200 pair draws; 7,680 fresh actions; 360 updates for each network; 23,040 reused action records; 0 token training units.
verification.observed: All exact counts matched. Final logged steps were SFT 60, RM 300 and PPO rollout 120. The first trace contains three epochs of the same 64 records.
verification.details: The maximum advantage error is 5.9605e-8 and ratio error 6.0840e-8, both below 2e-7. Old logs, values, rewards, advantages and hashes stay fixed across the reuse epochs.
